result.title: GeoEdit: Adversarial De-Evidencing for Silent Geoprivacy Protection via Image Editing
result.summary: Recent efforts have demonstrated the strong capabilities of Multimodal Large Reasoning Models (MLRMs) in geographic reasoning. By jointly analyzing subtle visual cues, these models can infer the locations of photos, thus enabling doxing even by non-expert adversaries. Existing defense methods struggle to balance the shareability of photos with effective protection, and often fail to sufficiently disrupt the implicit geo-evidence chains embedded in scene semantics. To this end, we propose GeoEdit, an adversarial de-evidencing framework for silent geoprivacy protection via image editing. Specifically, we apply minimal edits to high-risk evidence anchors in the image, thereby disrupting the underlying spatial reasoning chains while preserving overall scene semantics. We identify these anchors by combining structured knowledge with adversarially discovered geographic cues. To further navigate the large editing action space, we adopt a learnable policy to iteratively refine editing decisions, distilling successful trajectories into transferable natural-language insights for consistent and efficient editing. Evaluated on LifePhotoBench, GeoEdit achieves strong protection against 6 mainstream MLRMs, outperforming visual perturbation baselines by over 0.59 in image fidelity.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 GeoEdit，对图像中高风险「证据锚点」做最小编辑，以破坏 MLRM 地理定位所依赖的隐式证据链，同时保留整体场景语义；并用可学习策略迭代优化编辑决策，将成功轨迹蒸馏为自然语言经验。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「证据锚点/证据链」视角直接涉及哪些视觉细节支撑多模态推理，可供核查视觉证据筛选与视觉旁路问题；但目标是隐私保护而非 latent 状态生成，需确认编辑作用于输入证据而非内部表示。
